notes:
### Apportionment Formula
* **Fact:** New Jersey uses a **single sales factor** (a 100% weighted receipts fraction) to apportion multistate operational business income. The allocation factor is computed as New Jersey receipts divided by receipts everywhere and must be carried to six decimal places (e.g., `0.123456`).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax year 2025 and tax year 2026 (no statutory change between these years).
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/cbt/overview.shtml
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/cbt/cbt100i.pdf
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/tb/tb112r.pdf

---

### Sourcing for Services and Intangibles
* **Services:** Sourced using **market-based sourcing**. Receipts from services are allocated to New Jersey if the benefit of the service is received in New Jersey (cost of performance is not used). 
* **Intangibles:** Sourced based on location of use or commercial domicile:
  * Royalties from patents, copyrights, and trademarks are sourced to New Jersey if used within the State.
  * Receipts from sales of intangible assets / capital assets are sourced based on the net gain recognized rather than gross selling price (or included at gross receipts if the business regularly buys and sells securities or intangible assets for trading purposes).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax year 2025 and tax year 2026 (no change between these years).
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/tb/tb112r.pdf
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/tb/tb108r.pdf
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/cbt/b&fi.pdf

---

### Industries with Their Own Apportionment Formula
New Jersey provides specific apportionment rules and sourcing formulas for several distinct industries:
* **Airlines:** Pursuant to N.J.S.A. 54:10A-6.3, transportation revenues are apportioned based on the ratio of revenue miles in New Jersey to total revenue miles. If an airline engages in passenger transport, freight transport, and aircraft leasing, it calculates a weighted average of passenger, freight, and rental revenue mile fractions.
* **Freight Transportation Companies (Air or Ground in Combined Groups):** Pursuant to N.J.S.A. 54:10A-4.7(b), if 50% or more of the combined group's entire net income is derived from freight transportation, income is apportioned based on **ton-miles** traveled in New Jersey divided by total ton-miles everywhere.
* **Special Sourcing Rule Industries (N.J.A.C. 18:7-8.10A):** Specific market-sourcing rules govern:
  * Asset management / financial services (sourced based on investor/customer domicile);
  * Advertising services;
  * Casino / gaming industries (net gaming receipts reported under GAAP).
* **Regulated Investment Companies (RICs) & Investment Companies:** May qualify for special statutory apportionment percentages (e.g., fixed allocation percentages).
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax year 2025 and tax year 2026 (casinos updated June 2025; no changes between 2025 and 2026).
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/cbt/cbt100ui.pdf
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/tb/tb112r.pdf

---

### Apportionment Schedule / Form
* **Fact:** 
  * **Schedule J (Computation of Allocation Factor):** Used on **Form CBT-100** (Corporation Business Tax Return for C corporations) and **Form CBT-100S** (for S corporations).
  * **Schedule J (Computation of Group Allocation Factor):** Used on **Form CBT-100U** for combined groups.
  * *(Unincorporated/pass-through entities use Form NJ-NR-A or Schedule J of Form NJ-1065).*
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax year 2025 and tax year 2026.
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/cbt/cbt100.pdf
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/cbt/cbt100i.pdf
  * https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/cbt/cbt100ui.pdf

notes:
### 1. Corporation Business Tax (CBT / Income & Franchise Tax) Nexus

* **Nexus Standards:**
  * Domestic corporations are subject to CBT for the privilege of existing under the laws of New Jersey.
  * Foreign corporations have nexus if they:
    * Hold a Certificate of Authority or other department/agency authorization to engage in corporate activity in NJ;
    * Do business in NJ;
    * Employ or own capital or property in NJ;
    * Maintain an office or a stock of goods in NJ;
    * Derive receipts from NJ sources meeting bright-line economic nexus thresholds;
    * Engage in contacts/contracts within NJ; or
    * Act as a partner in a partnership doing business in NJ.
* **Bright-Line Economic Nexus Threshold:**
  * Enacted by P.L. 2023, c. 96 (N.J.S.A. 54:10A-2), a corporation is deemed to have bright-line economic nexus if during its tax year:
    * Receipts derived from New Jersey sources exceed **$100,000**; **or**
    * **200 or more separate transactions** are delivered to customers in New Jersey.
  * A corporation that does not meet either threshold and does not establish nexus via physical/other contacts does not have CBT nexus, even if it has New Jersey receipts.
* **Applicability:** Applies to privilege periods ending on and after July 31, 2023, including **Tax Years 2025 and 2026** (no change between 2025 and 2026).
* **Official Sources:**
  * NJ Division of Taxation Technical Bulletin TB-108(R): https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/tb/tb-108.pdf
  * NJ Form CBT-100 Instructions: https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/current/cbt/cbt100i.pdf

---

### 2. Remote Seller Economic Nexus Threshold (Sales and Use Tax)

* **Economic Nexus Threshold:**
  A remote seller without physical presence that makes retail sales of tangible personal property, specified digital products, or taxable services delivered into New Jersey must register, collect, and remit NJ Sales Tax if it meets either criterion:
  * Gross revenue from sales of tangible personal property, specified digital products, or taxable services delivered into New Jersey exceeds **$100,000**; **or**
  * The seller makes **200 or more separate transactions** of tangible personal property, specified digital products, or taxable services delivered into New Jersey.
* **Measurement Period:**
  * Measured based on the **current or prior calendar year**.
  * Once the threshold is met, the obligation to collect Sales Tax applies for the remainder of the current calendar year and the entirety of the following calendar year. (A grace period of up to 30 calendar days is allowed to complete registration and begin collection after the threshold is reached).
* **Applicability:** Established under P.L. 2018, c. 131; fully applies to **Tax Years 2025 and 2026** without change.
* **Official Sources:**
  * NJ Sales Tax Remote Sellers Frequently Asked Questions: https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/remotesellers.shtml
  * NJ Division of Taxation Publication ANJ-27 (*Making Mail-Order and Internet Sales*): https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/sales/anj27.pdf

---

### 3. State Position on Public Law 86-272 Protection

* **General Rule & Protected Activities:**
  * P.L. 86-272 (15 U.S.C. § 381) prohibits New Jersey from imposing the net income tax component of the CBT if a corporation’s sole activity within New Jersey consists of soliciting orders for sales of tangible personal property, provided orders are sent outside NJ for approval and filled from points outside the state.
  * Protection applies strictly to sales of **tangible personal property**; it does not protect sales of services, intangibles, digital assets/financial products, or real estate.
* **Adoption of Revised MTC Guidance on Internet Activities:**
  * For privilege periods ending on and after July 31, 2023, New Jersey explicitly adopted the Multistate Tax Commission’s (MTC) revised statement of information regarding P.L. 86-272.
  * Under Division guidance (TB-108(R)), business interactions via the internet frequently exceed P.L. 86-272 immunity (e.g., placing targeted advertising cookies/apps, transmitting electronic code/instructions to repair or upgrade products, offering online post-sale warranty service, interactive customer chat/assistance, or inventory placed in marketplace facilitator fulfillment centers in NJ). Maintaining a static website allowing customers to search, review, order, and pay for tangible goods remains protected.
* **Return Filing and Minimum Tax Requirement:**
  * Entities protected under P.L. 86-272 that have nexus (including economic nexus) or are registered in NJ are **not** exempt from CBT filing obligations and remain subject to the **statutory minimum tax**.
  * Such corporations must file Form CBT-100 (or CBT-100S), check the P.L. 86-272 box, attach Schedule N (*Nexus – Immune Activity Declaration*), and include the Division's Nexus Questionnaire. P.L. 86-272 filers are exempt from the net income component and the Corporate Transit Fee.
* **Combined Groups (Finnigan Rule):**
  * For privilege periods ending on and after July 31, 2023, the combined group is treated as one taxpayer. If any member of the group exceeds P.L. 86-272 protection or engages in non-protected activities in New Jersey, the combined group loses P.L. 86-272 protection.
* **Applicability:** Applies to **Tax Years 2025 and 2026** (no change between 2025 and 2026).
* **Official Sources:**
  * NJ Division of Taxation Technical Bulletin TB-108(R): https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/tb/tb-108.pdf
  * NJ Division of Taxation Bulletin TB-79(R): https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pdf/pubs/tb/tb-79.pdf
  * NJ Division of Taxation Policy Notice on Combined Groups and P.L. 86-272: https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/cbt-pl86-272.shtml

notes:
### 1. Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets

New Jersey imposes a graduated Gross Income Tax. The tax rates and brackets are unchanged between tax year 2025 and tax year 2026.

#### **Table A: Single; Married/CU Partner Filing Separate Return**
* **$0 to $20,000:** 1.4%
* **$20,000 to $35,000:** 1.75%
* **$35,000 to $40,000:** 3.5%
* **$40,000 to $75,000:** 5.525%
* **$75,000 to $500,000:** 6.37%
* **$500,000 to $1,000,000:** 8.97%
* **Over $1,000,000:** 10.75%

#### **Table B: Married/CU Couple Filing Joint Return; Head of Household; Qualifying Widow(er)/Surviving CU Partner**
* **$0 to $20,000:** 1.4%
* **$20,000 to $50,000:** 1.75%
* **$50,000 to $70,000:** 2.45%
* **$70,000 to $80,000:** 3.5%
* **$80,000 to $150,000:** 5.525%
* **$150,000 to $500,000:** 6.37%
* **$500,000 to $1,000,000:** 8.97%
* **Over $1,000,000:** 10.75%

*Note on Nonresident Composite Returns (Form NJ-1080-C):* Taxed at a flat rate of 10.75%.

* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit_taxrates.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/njit_taxrates.shtml)

---

### 2. Corporate Income / Franchise Tax Rates & Minimum Tax

The New Jersey Corporation Business Tax (CBT) Act imposes a franchise tax measured by entire net income allocable to New Jersey. The rates and minimum tax schedules are unchanged between tax year 2025 and tax year 2026.

#### **CBT Net Income Tax Rates**
* **Entire Net Income over $100,000:** 9.0%
* **Entire Net Income greater than $50,000 and up to $100,000:** 7.5%
* **Entire Net Income of $50,000 or less:** 6.5%

#### **Corporate Transit Fee (Surtax/Fee)**
* **Rate:** 2.5%
* **Threshold & Applicability:** Imposed on corporations with taxable net income exceeding $10,000,000. Public utility companies and New Jersey S corporations are exempt.
* **Applicable Privilege Periods:** Tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2024 through December 31, 2028 (applies to both TY 2025 and TY 2026).

#### **Minimum Tax Schedule (Based on New Jersey Gross Receipts)**
* **Gross receipts less than $100,000:** $500
* **Gross receipts equal to or greater than $100,000, but less than $250,000:** $750
* **Gross receipts equal to or greater than $250,000, but less than $500,000:** $1,000
* **Gross receipts equal to or greater than $500,000, but less than $1,000,000:** $1,500
* **Gross receipts equal to or greater than $1,000,000:** $2,000
* **Affiliated/controlled groups:** $2,000 for each member of a group with a total payroll of $5,000,000 or more.

* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:** 
  * [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/corprates.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/corprates.shtml)
  * [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/transitfee.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/transitfee.shtml)

---

### 3. Sales and Use Tax Rate & Local Sales Taxes

* **State Sales and Use Tax Rate:** 6.625% across the State. Unchanged for 2025 and 2026.
* **Local Sales Taxes:** New Jersey has a single statewide sales tax rate, and local jurisdictions do not enact broad local sales taxes. However, specific statutory localized rates and adjustments apply to certain transactions:
  * **Atlantic City:** Specific retail sales (entertainment, admission, rolling chairs, and room rentals) are subject to a 9% Atlantic City Luxury Tax and a reduced 3.625% New Jersey Sales Tax (12.625% combined rate). Alcoholic beverages sold by the drink are subject to a combined rate of 9.625% (3% Atlantic City Luxury Tax + 6.625% State Sales Tax).
  * **Cape May County (Wildwood, Wildwood Crest, North Wildwood):** A 2% Tourism Sales Tax applies to tourism-related sales (predominantly restaurant dining, hotel/lodging, and amusement admissions) in addition to the 6.625% State Sales Tax.
  * **Urban Enterprise Zones (UEZ) & Salem County:** Certain qualified retail sales of tangible personal property made in person by certified sellers are charged at 50% of the regular rate (3.3125%).

* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:** 
  * [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/salestaxrates.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/salestaxrates.shtml)
  * [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/luxury.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/luxury.shtml)

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes

* **Corporation Business Tax Franchise Requirement:** CBT is legally structured as a franchise tax for the privilege of exercising a corporate franchise or doing business in the state.
* **Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax (PTE/BAIT):** An elective entity-level tax on pass-through entities (partnerships, LLCs, S corporations). 
  * **Brackets & Rates:**
    * $0 to $250,000: 5.675%
    * $250,001 to $1,000,000: 6.52%
    * Over $1,000,000: 10.9%
  * *Applicable Tax Years:* 2025 and 2026.
  * *Official URL:* [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pba_it.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/pba_it.shtml)
* **Partnership Filing Fee:** 
  * Partnerships and LLCs classified as partnerships with more than two partners and New Jersey source income/loss must pay a filing fee of $150 per owner/partner (capped at $250,000 per year), plus a mandatory 50% installment prepayment for the subsequent privilege period.
  * *Applicable Tax Years:* 2025 and 2026.
  * *Official URL:* [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/partnershipprepay.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/partnershipprepay.shtml)
* **Petroleum Products Gross Receipts Tax (PPGRT):** 
  * Imposed on gross receipts/consideration and gallonage from the first sale of petroleum products in New Jersey.
  * Rates include statutory gross receipts percentage assessments and cents-per-gallon equivalent components adjusted semi-annually/annually by the Division of Taxation.
  * *Applicable Tax Years:* 2025 and 2026.
  * *Official URL:* [https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/petroleum.shtml](https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/petroleum.shtml)

notes:
### Individual Returns (Calendar-Year Filers) & Extension Rules
* **Due Date:** Calendar-year individual gross income tax returns are due on **April 15** following the close of the tax year (e.g., April 15, 2026, for tax year 2025; April 15, 2027, for tax year 2026).
* **Extension Period:** A **6-month extension** to file is granted (to October 15). 
* **Extension Requirements:** 
  * Taxpayers must pay at least **80%** of their actual New Jersey tax liability by the original April 15 due date.
  * If applying for a federal extension (Form 4868) and at least 80% of the NJ liability is satisfied by withholdings/estimated payments, a separate state extension is not required; enclose a copy of the federal application when filing.
  * If a payment is needed to meet the 80% threshold, or if no federal extension was requested, file **Form NJ-630** (or file online) with payment by April 15.
  * An extension grants extra time to file only, not to pay; late payment interest and penalties apply to unpaid tax after the original due date.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** Tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URL:** https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/when-file.shtml

---

### Corporate & Pass-Through Return Due Dates and Extension Rules
* **C-Corporations (Form CBT-100 / CBT-100U):**
  * *Due Date:* Due on the 15th day of the month following the federal due date—for calendar-year filers, this is **May 15**.
  * *Extension:* A **6-month extension** (to November 15) is granted using **Form CBT-200-T** (filed and paid electronically). At least **90%** of the corporate tax liability must be paid by the original due date.
* **S-Corporations (Form CBT-100S):**
  * *Due Date:* Due 30 days after the federal S corporation deadline—for calendar-year filers, this is **April 15**.
  * *Extension:* A **6-month extension** (to October 15) is requested using **Form CBT-200-T**. Requires at least **90%** of the tax liability to be paid by the original due date.
* **Partnerships (Form NJ-1065 / NJ-CBT-1065):**
  * *Due Date:* Due on the 15th day of the fourth month after the close of the tax year (**April 15** for calendar-year filers).
  * *Extension:* A **5-month extension** (to September 15). If a federal extension (Form 7004) is granted, an automatic 5-month extension applies to Form NJ-1065. If a partnership filing fee is due, the entity must file **Form PART-200-T** and pay at least **80%** of the fee by April 15. If nonresident partner tax is owed on Form NJ-CBT-1065, file **Form CBT-206** with at least **90%** of the tax paid by April 15.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** Tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * CBT Due Dates: https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/cbt_due_date.shtml
  * Partnership Rules: https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/partnfee.shtml

---

### Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTE/BAIT)
* **Existence:** Yes; the New Jersey Pass-Through Business Alternative Income Tax (PTE/BAIT) allows partnerships, LLCs, and S corporations with at least one member subject to NJ Gross Income Tax to elect to pay tax at the entity level.
* **Tax Rates (Graduated on Total Distributive Proceeds):**
  * $0 – $250,000: **5.675%**
  * $250,001 – $1,000,000: **6.52%**
  * $1,000,001 – $5,000,000: **9.12%**
  * Over $5,000,000: **10.9%**
* **How and When to Elect:**
  * Must register with the Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services and submit the election annually online through the Division of Taxation’s PTE File and Pay System.
  * *Election Deadline:* Must be made annually on or before the original due date of the return (**March 15** for calendar-year filers); cannot be made retroactively.
* **Return & Extension:** Annual return is filed on **Form PTE-100** by March 15. A **6-month extension** (to September 15) is requested via **Form PTE-200-T** online with at least **80%** of the tax liability paid.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** Tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URL:** https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/ptrp/bait.shtml

---

### Composite or Group Nonresident Returns
* **Return Form & Election:** Qualified entities can file a composite return on **Form NJ-1080-C**. Each participant must execute **Form NJ-1080-E** (Election to Participate in a Composite Return), kept on file by the entity.
* **Eligibility:** Nonresident individuals only who have no New Jersey-source income other than from the filing entity (or other composite filings), have no permanent place of abode in NJ, and waive deductions and exemptions.
* **Tax Rate:** Computed at the highest personal Gross Income Tax rate: flat **10.75%**.
* **Due Date & Extension:** Due **April 15** for calendar-year entities. A **6-month extension** (to October 15) is requested on **Form NJ-630** under the entity’s FEIN, provided at least **80%** of the tax is paid by the original due date.
* **Filing Specifications:** Form NJ-1080-C is filed on paper; entities with **25 or more** participants must submit participant directories on rewritable CD/diskette or approved electronic medium.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** Tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URL:** https://www.nj.gov/treasury/taxation/taxrates.shtml

---

### Estimated Tax Requirements & Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Throughs
* **Individual Estimated Taxes (Form NJ-1040-ES):**
  * Required if expected New Jersey Gross Income Tax liability exceeds withholdings and credits by more than **$400**.
  * *Payment Schedule (Calendar Filers):* Four installments due **April 15, June 15, September 15**, and **January 15** of the following year.
  * *Safe Harbor:* Underpayment interest is avoided if payments equal at least **80%** of the current tax liability or **100%** of the prior year's tax liability.
* **PTE/BAIT Estimated Taxes (Form PTE-150):**
  * Required if total estimated tax liability exceeds **$400**.
  * Installments are due on the 15th day of the 4th, 6th, and 9th months of the tax year and the 1st month following year-end (April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15).
  * Safe harbor threshold to avoid interest: at least **80%** of current year tax or **100%** of prior year tax.
* **Nonresident Partner Withholding / Remittance (Form NJ-CBT-1065):**
  * Partnerships must remit tax on behalf of nonresident partners' allocable share of NJ income:
    * Nonresident noncorporate partners (individuals, trusts, estates): **6.37%**.
    * Nonresident corporate partners: **9%**.
  * *Partnership Filing Fee:* Partnerships with more than 2 partners and NJ-source income/loss pay **$150 per owner** (up to a maximum of **$250,000**), plus a **50% prepayment** toward the next tax year.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** Tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:**
